turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through, mind the step. Clinic's running late, I'm sorry. What's brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, it's this burning on my chest. One side. And a few blisters. I've been worrying myself sick about it.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm Dawn, I come in weekday mornings. He's been pacing the kitchen, wouldn't even have his tea.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Whereabouts is the burning, and how long has it been going?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Left side. Err, two days, the burning and the blisters both. Like a hot cup held on the skin.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two days, left side. Are the blisters in one patch?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, just a little cluster. I had chickenpox as a kid, terribly, is it that again? Sorry, I'm jumping ahead.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll come to that. Any fever?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I keep touching my forehead though, like a fool.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Coughing at all?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): And shortness of breath with it?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Never.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is the rash itchy?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. What medicines do you take, day to day?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine for the pressure, five milligrams, in the morning. The cholesterol one at night, um, atorvastin, twenty milligrams. Sugar tablets for the sugar, metformin, 500 milligrams in the morning and with my tea. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, I couldn't tell you the proper name.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The powder's just a brown tin from his sister in Leicester. I put it by his cup, he does take it.

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, and I stopped the naproxen in March. That was two hundred and fifty milligrams twice a day, played havoc with my stomach. They wanted ramipril as well but I never took it.

[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): So that's amlodipine five milligrams each morning for the pressure, atorvastatin twenty milligrams at night, metformin five hundred morning and with your tea, plus that powder. Naproxen stopped in March, ramipril never started. With the pressure, any headaches?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes, if I've been rushing about.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any puffiness round the ankles?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that either.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, let's have a look. Shirt up, that's it.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): There's a small crop of blisters on the left chest, stopping at the midline, and a bit of redness round them. Chest is clear and I can't hear a murmur.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is 78. Blood pressure today is 136 over 84.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it my heart though? My brother had a heart attack at sixty. I parked on a double yellow I was that worked up, that's not important, sorry.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): I don't think this is your heart. One-sided burning, blisters that respect the midline, and chickenpox as a child. My working impression is shingles.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Shingles? Oh god. Is it catching? My daughter-in-law's pregnant, she's meant to come tomorrow. Can she still come? Will I give it to the baby?
[SEG0030] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Priya, yes, about six months gone. He was saving her a slice of cake and everything.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Best she stays away while the blisters are weeping. Once they've crusted, the risk is much lower. Keep the rash covered, and don't share towels.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, actually, it does itch. Quite a lot once I'm in bed, round the blisters. I said no before, that wasn't right.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's fine, itching fits. I'm starting an antiviral today, aciclovir, 800 milligrams five times a day for seven days, by mouth.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Five times a day? Will it clash with the amlodipine? Will it make me sick? And how long does the burning last?

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): It doesn't clash with your amlodipine, or the others. Have it with a little food if your stomach's delicate. The burning often settles over the week, though it can grumble on after the spots dry.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I have to stay indoors the whole time? And what if blisters pop up on the other side? Should I stop the Ayurvedic powder?

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): You needn't shut yourself away, just avoid Priya, and babies or anyone very run down, until it crusts. If it spreads across the midline or you feel very poorly, ring us sooner. I'd pause the powder this week, we don't know what's in it, but carry on with the amlodipine, the atorvastatin and the metformin.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. A week of not knowing feels awful, will you actually see me again?
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll book you back in a week, face to face, so I can check the rash myself.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Of. Sorry for all the questions. I just keep picturing the baby.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're alright. Covered rash, Priya stays away till the blisters crust, aciclovir five times a day for seven days, and I'll see you in a week.

spec.situation: Older person with burning pain on one side of the chest and a few blisters for two days; remembers chickenpox as a child; doctor prescribes antiviral today and gives infection advice about contact with a pregnant relative.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

bad.reason: Patient said 'Not really,' not a definite absence of cough.
Transcript says 'ring us sooner,' not explicitly a consultation.
bad.text: consultation (time_reference=value: if it spreads across the midline or you feel very poorly, status=conditional)

omissions.text: Rash was described by the patient as a little cluster / in one patch on the left side.
Past history of chickenpox in childhood was stated by the patient.
Naproxen was stopped in March because it 'played havoc' with his stomach.
Ramipril had been recommended but the patient never took it.

Headache history is recorded misleadingly: the patient first said no, then qualified that he only sometimes gets headaches if rushing about, in response to a blood-pressure review, not as a presenting symptom.
The patient initially denied itch but then corrected himself that the rash does itch quite a lot, especially when in bed.
Doctor advised that aciclovir does not clash with amlodipine or the patient's other medicines.
Doctor advised to take aciclovir with a little food if the patient's stomach is delicate.
Doctor counselled that the burning often settles over the week but can persist after the spots dry.
Doctor advised the patient need not stay indoors / shut himself away, only to avoid Priya, babies, or anyone very run down until the rash crusts.
Follow-up was specified as face to face in one week so the doctor can check the rash personally.
